reasoning: Two faults present. (1) plane_signal_mm=45: forty-five millimetres of signal trace running on the GND-plane layer carves a slot-antenna discontinuity into the return-current path; every net above that slot sees elevated common-mode impedance and radiated emissions risk. This fault is physically sourced — it is a routing-layer-assignment error, not a trace-width error — so the current scorer does not price it at all; candidates with heavy plane carving score identically to clean ones. (2) kelvin_ok=false: the Kelvin hard gate already fires, so the candidate is rejected, but the gate alone gives the manager no gradient information — it cannot distinguish 'one sense net stranded' from 'all six stranded'. Adding a scalar proxy (plane_signal_mm) to the score gives the manager a continuous signal to minimise on the way to clearing the gate, guiding it toward shallower plane cuts that also tend to free the stranded Kelvin tap.

scorer_penalty.rationale: Subtract 0.8 objective points per mm of signal copper on the GND-plane layer. The threshold is 0 (any plane carving is penalised). The penalty is additive to the existing objective() so it does not alter the kelvin/diffpair hard-gate logic; it merely ranks candidates with less plane carving higher within the gate-failing pool, giving the repair loop a descent direction toward the simultaneous fix of kelvin_ok (stranded sense taps are usually caused by the same plane cuts that drive plane_signal_mm up).

manager_rule: If kelvin_ok=false AND plane_signal_mm > 10, instruct the worker to reassign all signal nets currently on the GND-plane layer to the signal layer (F.Cu or B.Cu) before the next Freerouting pass, and add a rule-area KEEP-OUT on the GND inner plane for the bounding box of each cable corridor; do not attempt via insertion or trace widening until plane carving is eliminated, because via fields into a carved plane compound the return-path discontinuity and will not recover the stranded Kelvin tap.
